steps.action: Audit current schemas/validators/encoders and classify breaking vs compatibility-only changes, including stricter coercion hotspots and the 2 tax-service validator endpoints.

steps.action: Publish the exact v2 OpenAPI artifact and regenerate @acme/payments-client@2.x plus the mobile SDK from that artifact.

steps.action: Get mobile apps into a release-ready state and complete app-store submission so the new SDK is in user hands.

steps.action: Enable the server-side v2 compatibility path behind a feature flag, keeping dual-support for v1 and v2 clients without dropping legacy fields.
steps.rollback: disable the v2 schema/serialization flag and serve v1-compatible output

steps.action: Deploy the new server build in a business-hours canary and keep traffic small while measuring rejection rate and audit logs.

steps.action: If canary stays within baseline, expand rollout to production while preserving the dual-support shim until adoption thresholds are met.

steps.action: After 80% internal adoption and mobile release are confirmed, schedule the deprecation window for v1-only compatibility code and legacy field support.

01-safety-leaning.summary: Prepare v2 in code, publish v2 artifacts, ship mobile/client updates, then canary and dual-run server cutover with strict rollback gates.

steps.action: Create a migration branch and inventory all Pydantic/FastAPI touchpoints: validators, root validators, json_encoders, orm_mode models, .dict/.json call sites, and the two tax-service validators.
steps.rollback: delete migration branch and revert inventory notes
steps.observability: Counted migration surface, endpoint list, and risk hotspots for strict coercion and async validator behavior

steps.action: Run bump-pydantic codemod across the codebase, then manually rewrite the 6 root validators, 3 custom serializers, and 12 orm_mode models to v2 patterns.
steps.rollback: revert codemod changes and restore pre-migration model code
steps.observability: Build/test failures, model serialization diffs, validator ordering regressions, and any missing serializer coverage

steps.action: Replace remaining .dict()/.json() usage with .model_dump()/.model_dump_json(), then add targeted compatibility shims for any legacy response shapes still needed by v1 consumers.
steps.rollback: restore prior dump calls and compatibility shims from version control
steps.observability: Output payload diffs, JSON key ordering/nullability changes, and endpoint snapshot tests

steps.action: Refactor the two tax-service validators to remove async-in-validator behavior by moving remote calls into the request path or dependency layer, and rotate any touched secrets before enabling the new path.
steps.rollback: restore previous secret version and revert validator-path refactor
steps.observability: Tax-service call success rate, latency, error handling, and audit-log coverage

steps.action: Run baseline traffic characterization on v1 for the strict-coercion-sensitive endpoints, identify bodies that would fail under v2, and decide explicit non-strict relaxations for accepted cases.
steps.rollback: disable new validation path and redeploy_previous
steps.observability: Validation rejection delta, field-level coercion failures, and endpoint-specific rejection samples

steps.action: Regenerate OpenAPI from the v2 code, review schema diffs, publish the signed-off v2 OpenAPI artifact, and generate the TypeScript client v2 plus mobile SDK artifacts from that exact schema.
steps.rollback: withdraw_v2_artifacts_and_republish_v1_artifacts
steps.observability: OpenAPI diff report, generated client incompatibilities, nullable/discriminator changes, and SDK build outputs

steps.action: Publish @acme/payments-client@2.x and release the updated mobile SDKs to app stores, keeping server behavior on v1-compatible output during the mixed-fleet period.
steps.rollback: revert client publish and mobile SDK release artifacts
steps.observability: Package publication status, app store submission/review state, and consumer download/adoption signals

steps.action: Send partner/integrator notices and release-manager approvals for the upcoming migration window, including docs-site and externally visible schema-change communication.
steps.rollback: revert docs/client publish and redeploy_previous
steps.observability: Notice delivery confirmation, escalation intake readiness, and comms approval trail

steps.action: Deploy the FastAPI 0.110 + Pydantic v2 server behind a feature flag that preserves v1-compatible serialization and validation behavior for all external callers.
steps.rollback: disable the v2 schema/serialization flag and serve v1-compatible output
steps.observability: Canary error rate, validation rejection rate, audit-log completeness, latency, and any schema-diff-driven response changes

steps.action: Run business-hours canary rollout with staged traffic increase, holding the deploy if validation rejection exceeds baseline or audit events go missing.
steps.gate: window:business-hours excluding Friday afternoon and incident windows
steps.rollback: shift traffic back to FastAPI 0.95.2 + Pydantic v1 deployment
steps.observability: Canary p99 latency, rejection-rate delta, audit log missing events, tax-service validator failures, and end-to-end payment success

steps.action: Maintain dual-support for v1 and v2 clients in production, with the compatibility shim left enabled until internal adoption and mobile rollout are safely complete.
steps.rollback: restore v1-compatible request/response handling
steps.observability: Client version mix, v1 fallback usage, mobile app version distribution, and legacy field usage

steps.action: After 80% internal adoption and mobile SDKs are in user hands, remove the legacy compatibility path, retire deprecated fields only after a 30-day quiet period, and finalize the v2-only server contract.
steps.rollback: restore legacy fields and backfill missing values
steps.observability: Legacy field traffic, customer incidents, downstream parser errors, and long-tail consumer failures

Backend wants rollout of validator changes, while Security requires approval, audit-trail integrity, and secret rotation first for validator/tax-service changes.
Backend wants client/server changes shipped, while ProductPM requires partner notice, release-manager approval, customer escalation ownership, and non-launch-window rollout.
DataPlatform requires no legacy field drops until traffic is quiet, while ConsumerSubsystem requires preserving legacy compatibility until all critical services and mobile apps are on v2.

ConsumerSubsystem requires mobile SDK shipped and in user hands before cutover, while DataPlatform requires exact-schema-only artifact regeneration and sign-off before publishing client inputs.
